observations.text: SP, due to a formation briefing conducted without the CRM structure, did not cover the mission planning, communication and airmanship items for the planned formation profile, and the visual signals and the radio calls for each maneuver were left unbriefed. Throughout the flight the division of duties between the cockpits was not stated and the SP did not carry out the rejoin without assistance, with the result that the IP directed the geometry and executed part of the maneuver. The CRM box was checked only after the IP built the debriefing points on the SP's behalf.

SP, due to an unagreed division of lookout responsibility within the formation, did not use the CRM concept when analyzing the closure developing during the rejoin and did not pass the position relative to the flight lead to the front cockpit. The SP did not resolve the situation without assistance, with the result that the IP allocated the roles and executed part of the correction. During the debriefing the areas for CRM development were identified by the IP and not by the SP.

SP integrated CRM into the formation briefing and the debriefing at the level expected for the training section; however, the IFG/CRM matrix chart was used to highlight the particular items only after the IP's verbal prompts, on two occasions. The visual signals acknowledged to the flight lead were passed with delay each time they were required. Marginal performance for the training section - independent use of the CRM matrix chart, without prompting, is expected to improve.

SP integrated CRM into the formation briefing and the debriefing without the IP's prompting, using the IFG/CRM matrix chart to highlight the mission planning, communication and airmanship items of the formation profile. Minor omissions in verbalizing the position relative to the flight lead were recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention. The CRM concept was used when planning the maneuvers and the debriefing points were raised by the SP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP applied the CRM concept accurately and without delay in the formation briefing, throughout the flight and in the debriefing, and used the IFG/CRM matrix chart to highlight the mission planning, communication and airmanship items. The division of duties between the cockpits was stated before each formation maneuver and every deviation from the briefed plan was communicated to the flight lead as it was recognized, without the IP's intervention. The areas for CRM development were raised on the SP's own initiative during the debriefing. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated CRM performance above the desired level for the training section, integrating the CRM items into the formation briefing and the debriefing in a standardized manner and using the IFG/CRM matrix chart without any prompting. When the practice lost wingman condition was introduced, the SP stated the role allocation, requested the information needed from the front cockpit in plain language and analyzed the situation through the CRM concept before selecting the course of action. Coordination deviations across the sortie were negligible, and in the debriefing the SP set the areas for CRM development and solicited comments on where CRM enhanced mission effectiveness and flight safety. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to formation mission planning carried out without any CRM structure, did not brief the division of duties, the communication plan or the airmanship items for the planned formation profile. Throughout the flight the intentions of the two cockpits and of the flight were never consolidated and the SP did not complete the maneuver sequence without assistance, with the result that the IP directed each rejoin and executed part of the recovery. The CRM box was checked only after the IP conducted the debriefing points on the SP's behalf.

SP, due to a failure to make the knock-it-off call when the briefed formation parameters were exceeded, did not communicate the recognized deterioration of the geometry to the flight lead and did not analyze the situation through the CRM concept. The SP did not re-establish the briefed formation position without assistance, with the result that the IP made the call and took the aircraft for part of the separation maneuver. In the debriefing the SP identified the breakdown in communication only after the IP pointed it out.

SP, due to a formation briefing flow that omitted the IFG/CRM matrix chart, did not highlight the mission planning, communication and airmanship items applicable to the sortie. Throughout the flight the position relative to the flight lead and the intended next action were passed to the front cockpit only after the IP asked for them, on three occasions. The required formation calls were made with delay and the debriefing points were raised only after the IP's verbal prompts.

SP, due to a lack of assertiveness in requesting a repeat of the formation instruction that was not understood, did not confirm the directed maneuver with the flight lead before accepting it. The intentions of the flight were consolidated only after the IP prompted verbally for a read-back. Recognition of the communication lapse came with delay, and the areas for CRM improvement were reached in the debriefing only under the IP's guidance.

SP integrated the CRM items into the formation briefing, the flight and the debriefing within the standards of the training section; however, communication of the position relative to the flight lead twice lagged the actual change of geometry before the SP corrected it without the IP's intervention. The IFG/CRM matrix chart was used, but the airmanship subcategories were highlighted in less depth than the mission planning and communication items. Marginal performance for the training section - consistency in verbalizing the formation position at the moment of the change is expected to improve.

SP applied the CRM concept accurately and without delay when planning the formation maneuvers and when analyzing the simulated breakout, using the IFG/CRM matrix chart to highlight the mission planning, communication and airmanship items. Role assignment between the cockpits was stated before each formation maneuver and every change of position within the flight was verbalized without the IP's intervention. In the debriefing the SP identified the point at which CRM enhanced mission effectiveness and flight safety and proposed the areas for CRM development. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated CRM performance above the desired level for the training section, integrating the CRM items into the formation briefing and the debriefing in a standardized manner and using the IFG/CRM matrix chart without prompting. Under the increased workload of the practice lost wingman procedure the SP assigned the roles explicitly, requested the required information from the front cockpit in plain language and worked the problem as a crew rather than individually. Coordination deviations across the sortie were negligible and in the debriefing the SP solicited comments on where CRM enhanced mission effectiveness and flight safety. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a mission planning phase conducted without the CRM structure required for the formation profile, did not brief the division of duties, the communication plan or the airmanship items. Throughout the flight the two cockpits worked from different assumptions about the next formation maneuver and the SP did not complete the sequence without assistance. The IP directed the rejoin and executed part of the recovery, and the debriefing points were built by the IP and not by the SP.

SP, due to a failure to exercise the formation lead responsibilities after the lead change, did not state the intentions of the flight and did not use the CRM concept when planning the maneuvers that followed. The wingman was left without the required directive calls and the SP did not re-establish the briefed sequence without assistance. The IP allocated the roles and executed part of the maneuver, and the CRM box was checked only after the IP led the debriefing.

SP, due to a debriefing method that reviewed the formation maneuvers without reference to the IFG/CRM matrix chart, did not highlight the mission planning, communication and airmanship items of the sortie. Throughout the flight the required formation calls were passed only after the IP's verbal prompts and the coordination lapse was recognized with delay. The areas for CRM development were reached only after the IP directed the discussion toward them.

SP, due to absent plain-language cross-talk on the changing formation geometry, did not keep the mental models of the two cockpits consolidated during the maneuvering. The mismatch between the briefed position and the flown position was raised only after the IP prompted verbally, and the plan was corrected with delay. In the debriefing the SP described the communication breakdown only once the IP had structured the point.

SP, due to a formation briefing sequence that covered the communication plan after the maneuver descriptions instead of together with them, did not tie the required calls to the specific points of the profile. During the working phase two calls to the flight lead were passed late relative to the briefed points, and the SP recognized the mismatch and re-established the briefed communication flow without the IP's intervention. The CRM items were reviewed in the debriefing using the IFG/CRM matrix chart.

SP, due to a workload distribution that left the SP holding the formation position and transmitting at the same time, did not verbalize the change of the flight's geometry to the front cockpit at the point required. The omission was recognized by the SP shortly afterwards and the information was passed without the IP's intervention, so that the shared picture between the cockpits was restored. Minor coordination errors of this type occurred twice and were self-corrected in a timely manner.

SP applied the CRM concept in the formation briefing, throughout the flight and in the debriefing with the accuracy and the speed expected for the training section; however, the airmanship subcategories were highlighted on the IFG/CRM matrix chart only after a short pause on each occasion. Communication with the flight lead and with the front cockpit was correct in content, with the transmission of the position change made just inside the briefed timing. Marginal performance for the training section - a faster and more automatic use of the CRM matrix chart is expected to improve.

SP demonstrated CRM performance above the desired level for the training section, with the CRM items of mission planning, communication and airmanship integrated into the formation briefing and the debriefing in a standardized manner. Throughout the flight the role assignment was stated before every formation maneuver, the position relative to the flight lead was verbalized on each change of geometry and the SP used the IFG/CRM matrix chart to close the points carried forward from the previous debriefing. Coordination deviations were negligible and the SP identified, without any prompting, the phase in which CRM enhanced mission effectiveness and flight safety. Above end of block MIF achieved.
